# ProsemirrorEx.Authority

Source: https://prosemirror-ex.hexdocs.pm/ProsemirrorEx.Authority.md

# `ProsemirrorEx.Authority`
[🔗](https://github.com/yammine/prosemirror_ex/blob/main/lib/prosemirror_ex/authority.ex#L1)

Functional core for a collaborative editing authority server.

Holds the canonical document, receives steps from clients, validates versions,
applies steps, and provides step history for client catch-up.

This is a pure data structure with no process — use `ProsemirrorEx.Authority.Server`
for a GenServer wrapper.

# `doc`

Return the current document.

# `new`

Create a new Authority with the given schema and optional initial document.

If `doc` is nil, creates a minimal valid document using the schema's top node type.

# `receive_steps`

Receive steps from a client.

Steps must be pre-deserialized Step structs. The client's version must match
the authority's current version, otherwise `{:error, :version_mismatch}` is returned.

Returns:
- `{:ok, updated_authority}` on success
- `{:error, :version_mismatch}` if `client_version != authority.version`
- `{:error, :step_failed, message}` if a step fails to apply

# `steps_since`

Return steps and their client IDs from `since` to the current version.

Returns:
- `{:ok, steps, client_ids}` on success
- `{:error, :invalid_version}` if `since` is negative or beyond current version

# `version`

Return the current version.

---

*Consult [api-reference.md](api-reference.md) for complete listing*

---

# ProsemirrorEx.Authority.Server

Source: https://prosemirror-ex.hexdocs.pm/ProsemirrorEx.Authority.Server.md

# `ProsemirrorEx.Authority.Server`
[🔗](https://github.com/yammine/prosemirror_ex/blob/main/lib/prosemirror_ex/authority/server.ex#L1)

GenServer wrapper around `ProsemirrorEx.Authority`.

Handles JSON serialization/deserialization at the boundary so callers
work with plain maps. Suitable for integration with Phoenix channels,
LiveView, or any Elixir web framework.

## Usage

    {:ok, pid} = Authority.Server.start_link(schema: schema, doc: doc_node)

    # Receive steps from a client (steps as JSON maps)
    {:ok, new_version} = Authority.Server.receive_steps(pid, "client1", 0, [step_json])

    # Get the current document as JSON
    {doc_json, version} = Authority.Server.get_doc(pid)

    # Get step history since a version
    {:ok, steps_json, client_ids} = Authority.Server.steps_since(pid, 0)

# `child_spec`

Returns a specification to start this module under a supervisor.

See `Supervisor`.

# `get_doc`

Get the current document as JSON and the current version.

Returns `{doc_json, version}`.

# `receive_steps`

Submit steps from a client.

`steps_json` is a list of step JSON maps (as would arrive from a client).
Steps are deserialized, validated, and applied.

Returns `{:ok, new_version}` on success, or `{:error, reason}` / `{:error, reason, message}`.

# `start_link`

Start a linked Authority.Server process.

## Options

- `:schema` (required) - the ProseMirror schema
- `:doc` (optional) - initial document node
- `:name` (optional) - process name for registration

# `steps_since`

Get all steps since the given version as JSON maps.

Returns `{:ok, steps_json, client_ids}` or `{:error, reason}`.

---

*Consult [api-reference.md](api-reference.md) for complete listing*

---

# ProsemirrorEx.Model.ContentMatch

Source: https://prosemirror-ex.hexdocs.pm/ProsemirrorEx.Model.ContentMatch.md

# `ProsemirrorEx.Model.ContentMatch`
[🔗](https://github.com/yammine/prosemirror_ex/blob/main/lib/prosemirror_ex/model/content_match.ex#L1)

Instances of this struct represent a match state of a node type's
content expression, and can be used to find out whether further
content matches here, and whether a given position is a valid end
of the node.

Ported from ProseMirror's content.ts.

Because DFA states can form cycles (e.g., `image*` creates a state
with a self-loop), we use an ETS-backed registry to store the actual
edge lists. Each ContentMatch holds an `id` that indexes into this
registry. The `next` field is populated lazily from the registry.

# `compatible`

Whether this match state is compatible with another.

# `compute_wrapping`

Compute wrapping using BFS.

# `default_type`

Get the first matching node type that can be generated.

# `edge`

Get the nth outgoing edge as {type, next_match}.

# `edge_count`

The number of outgoing edges.

# `empty`

The empty content match (matches only empty content).

# `fill_before`

Try to match the given fragment, and if that fails, see if it can
be made to match by inserting nodes in front of it. When successful,
return a fragment of inserted nodes (which may be empty if nothing
had to be inserted). When `to_end` is true, only return a fragment
if the resulting match goes to the end of the content expression.

# `find_wrapping`

Find a set of wrapping node types that would allow a node of the
given type to appear at this position.

# `inline_content`

Whether the match state has inline content.

# `match_fragment`

Try to match a fragment. Returns the resulting match when successful.

# `match_type`

Match a node type, returning a match after that node if successful.

# `parse`

Parse a content expression string into a ContentMatch DFA.

`node_types` is a map of name => %NodeType{}.

# `update_node_types`

Update the node types stored in this content match's DFA edges.
Takes a map of name => updated_node_type. This is needed because
during schema construction, content expressions are parsed before
all node types have their content_match set, so the DFA edges
reference stale types.

---

*Consult [api-reference.md](api-reference.md) for complete listing*

---

# ProsemirrorEx.Model.Diff

Source: https://prosemirror-ex.hexdocs.pm/ProsemirrorEx.Model.Diff.md

# `ProsemirrorEx.Model.Diff`
[🔗](https://github.com/yammine/prosemirror_ex/blob/main/lib/prosemirror_ex/model/diff.ex#L1)

Finds the first and last differing positions between two fragments.

Ported from prosemirror-model's diff.ts.

# `find_diff_end`

Find the first position counting from the end at which the content of
two fragments diverges.

Returns `%{a: pos_a, b: pos_b}` or nil if they are identical.

# `find_diff_start`

Find the first position at which the content of two fragments diverges.

Returns the position or nil if they are identical.

---

*Consult [api-reference.md](api-reference.md) for complete listing*

# ProsemirrorEx.Model.Fragment

Source: https://prosemirror-ex.hexdocs.pm/ProsemirrorEx.Model.Fragment.md

# `ProsemirrorEx.Model.Fragment`
[🔗](https://github.com/yammine/prosemirror_ex/blob/main/lib/prosemirror_ex/model/fragment.ex#L6)

A fragment represents a node's collection of child nodes.

Like nodes, fragments are persistent data structures, and you should not
mutate them or their content. Rather, you create new instances whenever
needed. The API tries to make this easy.

# `t`

```elixir
@type t() :: %ProsemirrorEx.Model.Fragment{
  content: [ProsemirrorEx.Model.Node.t()],
  size: non_neg_integer()
}
```

# `add_to_end`

Add a node to the end of the fragment, joining it with the last child if possible.

# `add_to_start`

Add a node to the start of the fragment, joining it with the first child if possible.

# `append`

Concatenate two fragments, joining adjacent text nodes with the same
markup if possible.

# `child`

Get the child node at the given index. Raise an error when the index is
out of range.

# `child_count`

The number of child nodes in this fragment.

# `cut`

Cut out the sub-fragment between the two given positions.

Positions are document positions (not child indices). For text nodes,
positions map to character offsets. For non-text non-leaf nodes,
positions are adjusted by -1 to account for the opening token.

# `cut_by_index`

Cut by child index rather than position.

# `empty`

An empty fragment. Singleton.

# `eq`

Test whether this fragment is equal to another fragment.

# `find_diff_end`

Find the first position from the end at which the content of two fragments diverges.

# `find_diff_start`

Find the first position at which the content of two fragments diverges.

# `find_index`

Find the index and inner offset corresponding to a given document position.
Returns {index, offset}.

# `first_child`

Get the first child of this fragment, or nil.

# `fold_nodes_between`

Like `nodes_between/6` but threads an accumulator through each callback.

`f` receives `(node, start_pos, parent, index, acc)` and returns either:
- `acc` — descend into children with updated accumulator
- `{:skip, acc}` — skip children, continue with updated accumulator

# `for_each`

Call the given function for each child node, passing the node, its offset, and its index.

# `from`

Create a fragment from something that can be interpreted as a set of nodes.
For nil, it returns the empty fragment. For a fragment, the fragment itself
is returned. For a node or array of nodes, a fragment containing those
nodes is returned.

# `from_array`

Create a fragment from an array of nodes, joining adjacent text nodes
with the same markup.

# `from_json`

Deserialize a fragment from its JSON representation.

Takes a schema and either nil (returns empty fragment) or a list of node JSON maps.

# `last_child`

Get the last child of this fragment, or nil.

# `maybe_child`

Get the child node at the given index, if it exists.

# `new`

Create a new fragment with the given content and size.

# `nodes_between`

Call `f` for every descendant node between the given positions.

`f` receives `(node, start_pos, parent, index)`. When `f` returns `false`,
descending into that node is skipped.

# `replace_child`

Create a new fragment in which the node at the given index is replaced
by the given node.

# `text_between`

Extract the text between `from` and `to`. When `block_separator` is given,
it will be inserted between textblocks. When `leaf_text` is given, it will
be used to represent non-text leaf nodes (string or function).

# `to_json`

Serialize the content of this fragment to JSON. Returns nil if empty.

# `to_string_inner`

Join child debug strings with ", ".

---

*Consult [api-reference.md](api-reference.md) for complete listing*

---

# ProsemirrorEx.Model.Mark

Source: https://prosemirror-ex.hexdocs.pm/ProsemirrorEx.Model.Mark.md

# `ProsemirrorEx.Model.Mark`
[🔗](https://github.com/yammine/prosemirror_ex/blob/main/lib/prosemirror_ex/model/mark.ex#L1)

A mark is a piece of information that can be attached to a node, such as
it being emphasized, in code font, or a link. It has a type and optionally
a set of attributes that provide further information (such as the target of
the link). Marks are created through a Schema, which controls which types
exist and which attributes they have.

# `t`

```elixir
@type t() :: %ProsemirrorEx.Model.Mark{
  attrs: map(),
  type: ProsemirrorEx.Model.MarkType.t()
}
```

# `add_to_set`

```elixir
@spec add_to_set(t(), [t()]) :: [t()]
```

Add this mark to the given set, replacing any marks of the same type that
exist in it, and sorting it to match the order of marks in the schema.
Returns the input set when this mark is already in it.

Faithful port of the JS `addToSet` method.

# `eq`

```elixir
@spec eq(t(), t()) :: boolean()
```

Test whether this mark has the same type and attributes as another mark.

# `from_json`

Deserialize a mark from its JSON representation.

Takes a schema and a JSON map with `"type"` and optionally `"attrs"` keys.

# `is_in_set`

```elixir
@spec is_in_set(t(), [t()]) :: boolean()
```

Test whether this mark is in the given set of marks.
Returns true/false (matching JS Mark.prototype.isInSet).

# `none`

```elixir
@spec none() :: [t()]
```

The empty set of marks.

# `remove_from_set`

```elixir
@spec remove_from_set(t(), [t()]) :: [t()]
```

Remove this mark from the given set, returning the set itself if it isn't
found in it.

# `same_set`

```elixir
@spec same_set([t()], [t()]) :: boolean()
```

Test whether two sets of marks are identical.

# `set_from`

```elixir
@spec set_from([t()] | t() | nil) :: [t()]
```

Create a properly sorted mark set from null, a single mark, or an unsorted
array of marks.

# `to_json`

```elixir
@spec to_json(t()) :: map()
```

Serialize this mark to JSON.

---

*Consult [api-reference.md](api-reference.md) for complete listing*

---

# ProsemirrorEx.Model.MarkType

Source: https://prosemirror-ex.hexdocs.pm/ProsemirrorEx.Model.MarkType.md

# `ProsemirrorEx.Model.MarkType`
[🔗](https://github.com/yammine/prosemirror_ex/blob/main/lib/prosemirror_ex/model/mark_type.ex#L1)

A mark type is a specification for a type of mark in a schema.

# `t`

```elixir
@type t() :: %ProsemirrorEx.Model.MarkType{
  attrs: term(),
  excluded: term(),
  instance: term(),
  name: term(),
  rank: term(),
  schema: term(),
  spec: term()
}
```

# `check_attrs`

Validate attributes against the spec.

# `create`

Create a mark of this type. `attrs` may be nil or a map containing
only some of the mark's attributes. The others, if they have defaults,
will be added.

# `excludes`

Check whether this mark type excludes another.

# `is_in_set`

Tests whether there is a mark of this type in the given set. Returns the Mark or nil.

# `remove_from_set`

When there is a mark of this type in the given set, a new set without it is returned.

---

*Consult [api-reference.md](api-reference.md) for complete listing*

# ProsemirrorEx.Model.Node

Source: https://prosemirror-ex.hexdocs.pm/ProsemirrorEx.Model.Node.md

# `ProsemirrorEx.Model.Node`
[🔗](https://github.com/yammine/prosemirror_ex/blob/main/lib/prosemirror_ex/model/node.ex#L1)

Represents a ProseMirror document node. It holds a type,
optional attributes, a content Fragment, marks, and (for text nodes) text.

# `t`

```elixir
@type t() :: %ProsemirrorEx.Model.Node{
  attrs: term(),
  content: term(),
  marks: term(),
  text: term(),
  type: term()
}
```

# `can_append`

Test whether the given node's content can be appended to this node.
If that node's content is not empty, this is equivalent to checking
whether the content can be inserted at the end.

# `can_replace`

Test whether replacing the range `from..to` (child indices) in this
node with the given `replacement` fragment would leave the node's
content valid. `start` and `end_val` optionally restrict which part
of the replacement is considered.

# `can_replace_with`

Test whether replacing the range `from..to` (child indices) with a
node of the given `type` would leave the node's content valid.

# `check`

Check that this node's content is valid for its type.

Validates content against the content expression, checks that all
attributes are valid, and recursively checks children. Raises on
any validation error.

# `child`

Get the child node at the given index. Raises on out-of-range.

# `child_after`

Find the child node after the given position. Returns {node, index, offset}.

# `child_before`

Find the child node before the given position. Returns {node, index, offset}.

# `child_count`

The number of children that this node has.

# `children`

The list of children of this node.

# `content_match_at`

Return a content match state that represents the match after the
first `index` children of this node.

# `copy`

Create a copy of this node with the given content.

# `cut`

Cut the text or content of this node between the given positions.

# `debug_string`

A human-readable debug representation of this node (equivalent to JS toString).

# `descendants`

Call the given function for all descendant nodes.

# `eq`

Test whether this node is the same as another node (structurally equal).

# `first_child`

Get the first child of this node, or nil.

# `fold_descendants`

Fold over all descendant nodes, threading an accumulator.

`f` receives `(node, pos, parent, index, acc)` and returns either:
- `acc` — descend into children with updated accumulator
- `{:skip, acc}` — skip children, continue with updated accumulator

# `for_each`

Call `f` for each child node, passing (node, offset, index).

# `from_json`

Deserialize a node from its JSON representation.

Takes a schema and a JSON map. Handles text nodes specially.

# `has_markup`

Test whether this node has the given type, attributes, and marks.

# `inline_content`

True when this node allows inline content.

# `is_atom_node`

True when this is an atom node (a leaf node that is treated as a single unit).

# `is_block`

True when this is a block node.

# `is_inline`

True when this is an inline node.

# `is_leaf`

True when this is a leaf node.

# `is_text`

True when this is a text node.

# `is_textblock`

True when this is a textblock node (a block that contains inline content).

# `last_child`

Get the last child of this node, or nil.

# `mark`

Create a copy of this node with a different set of marks.

# `maybe_child`

Get the child node at the given index, or nil if out of range.

# `node_at`

Find the node at the given position.

# `node_size`

The size of this node as counted by the indexing scheme. For text nodes this is the text length, for leaf nodes it is 1, and for non-leaf nodes it is the content size + 2 (for the open and close tokens).

# `nodes_between`

Invoke a callback for all descendant nodes between the given positions
(relative to the start of this node's content). Passes the node, its
absolute position, its parent node, and its index into the parent's
child list.

When the callback returns `false`, descending into that node is skipped.

# `range_has_mark`

Test whether the given range contains a mark of the given type.

# `replace`

Replace a range of the document with the given slice.

# `resolve`

Resolve the given position in this document, returning a ResolvedPos.

# `same_markup`

Test whether the markup (type, attributes, marks) of this node is the same as that of another.

# `slice`

Extract a slice of the document between the given positions.

# `text_between`

Get the text between `from` and `to` positions within this node.

# `text_content`

Get the text content of this node.

# `to_json`

Serialize this node to JSON.

# `with_text`

Create a text node with the same type, attributes, and marks but different text.

---

*Consult [api-reference.md](api-reference.md) for complete listing*

---

# ProsemirrorEx.Model.NodeRange

Source: https://prosemirror-ex.hexdocs.pm/ProsemirrorEx.Model.NodeRange.md

# `ProsemirrorEx.Model.NodeRange`
[🔗](https://github.com/yammine/prosemirror_ex/blob/main/lib/prosemirror_ex/model/node_range.ex#L1)

Represents a flat range of content, i.e. one that starts and ends in the
same node.

Ported from ProseMirror's resolvedpos.ts (NodeRange class).

# `end_index`

The end index of the range in the parent node.

# `end_pos`

The position at the end of the range.

# `parent`

The parent node that the range points into.

# `start`

The position at the start of the range.

# `start_index`

The start index of the range in the parent node.

---

*Consult [api-reference.md](api-reference.md) for complete listing*

# ProsemirrorEx.Model.NodeType

Source: https://prosemirror-ex.hexdocs.pm/ProsemirrorEx.Model.NodeType.md

# `ProsemirrorEx.Model.NodeType`
[🔗](https://github.com/yammine/prosemirror_ex/blob/main/lib/prosemirror_ex/model/node_type.ex#L1)

A node type is a specification for a type of node in a schema.

# `allowed_marks`

Removes the marks that are not allowed in this node from the given set.

# `allows_mark_type`

Check whether this node type allows a given mark type.

# `allows_marks`

Test whether the given set of marks are allowed in this node.

# `check_attrs`

Validate attributes against the spec.

# `check_content`

Raises a RuntimeError if the given fragment is not valid content for this node type.

# `compatible_content`

Indicates whether this node allows some of the same content as the given node type.

# `compute_attrs`

Compute attrs, filling in defaults for missing values.

# `create`

Create a Node of this type. The given attributes are checked and
defaulted. `content` may be a Fragment, a node, an array of nodes,
or nil. Similarly `marks` may be nil to default to the empty set.
Does NOT check content against the content expression.

# `create_and_fill`

Like `create`, but see if it is necessary to add nodes to the start
or end of the given fragment to make it fit the node. If no fitting
wrapping can be found, return nil.

# `create_checked`

Like `create`, but check the given content against the node type's
content restrictions, and raise an error if it doesn't match.

# `has_required_attrs?`

Check whether this node type has any required attributes.

# `is_in_group`

Check whether this node type is in the given group.

# `valid_content`

Returns true if the given fragment is valid content for this node type.

# `whitespace`

Get the whitespace mode for this node type.

---

*Consult [api-reference.md](api-reference.md) for complete listing*

---

# `replace`

Replace the content between `$from` and `$to` with the given slice.

# ProsemirrorEx.Model.ResolvedPos

Source: https://prosemirror-ex.hexdocs.pm/ProsemirrorEx.Model.ResolvedPos.md

# `ProsemirrorEx.Model.ResolvedPos`
[🔗](https://github.com/yammine/prosemirror_ex/blob/main/lib/prosemirror_ex/model/resolved_pos.ex#L1)

Represents a resolved position in a ProseMirror document.

You can resolve a position to get more information about it. Objects of this
struct represent such a resolved position, providing various pieces of context
information, and some helper methods.

Throughout this module, functions that take an optional `depth` parameter
will interpret nil as `self.depth` and negative numbers as `self.depth + value`.

Ported from ProseMirror's resolvedpos.ts.

# `after_pos`

The (absolute) position directly after the wrapping node at the given level,
or the original position when `depth` is `self.depth + 1`.

# `before`

The (absolute) position directly before the wrapping node at the given level,
or, when `depth` is `self.depth + 1`, the original position.

# `block_range`

Returns a range based on the place where this position and the given
position diverge around block content.

# `doc`

The root node in which the position was resolved.

# `end_pos`

The (absolute) position at the end of the node at the given level.

# `index`

The index into the ancestor at the given level.

# `index_after`

The index pointing after this position into the ancestor at the given level.

# `marks`

Get the marks at this position, factoring in the surrounding marks'
`inclusive` property.

# `marks_across`

Get the marks after the current position, if any, except those that are
non-inclusive and not present at position `end_rpos`. This is mostly useful
for getting the set of marks to preserve after a deletion.

# `max`

Return the greater of this and the given position.

# `min`

Return the smaller of this and the given position.

# `node`

The ancestor node at the given level. `node(rpos, rpos.depth)` is the
same as `parent(rpos)`.

# `node_after`

Get the node directly after the position, if any. If the position points
into a text node, only the part of that node after the position is returned.

# `node_before`

Get the node directly before the position, if any. If the position points
into a text node, only the part of that node before the position is returned.

# `parent`

The parent node that the position points into.

# `pos_at_index`

Get the position at the given index in the parent node at the given depth
(which defaults to `self.depth`).

# `resolve`

Resolve the given position in the given document, returning a ResolvedPos.

# `resolve_depth`

Normalize a depth value. nil becomes self.depth, negative values
become self.depth + val.

# `same_parent`

Query whether the given position shares the same parent node.

# `shared_depth`

The depth up to which this position and the given (non-resolved) position
share the same parent nodes.

# `start`

The (absolute) position at the start of the node at the given level.

# `text_offset`

When this position points into a text node, this returns the distance
between the position and the start of the text node. Will be zero for
positions that point between nodes.

# `to_string`

String representation of this resolved position (for debugging).

---

*Consult [api-reference.md](api-reference.md) for complete listing*

---

# ProsemirrorEx.Model.Schema

Source: https://prosemirror-ex.hexdocs.pm/ProsemirrorEx.Model.Schema.md

# `ProsemirrorEx.Model.Schema`
[🔗](https://github.com/yammine/prosemirror_ex/blob/main/lib/prosemirror_ex/model/schema.ex#L1)

A document schema. Holds node and mark type objects for the nodes
and marks that may occur in conforming documents, and provides
functionality for creating and deserializing such documents.

Ported from ProseMirror's schema.ts.

# `mark`

Create a mark with the given type and attributes.

# `mark_from_json`

Deserialize a mark from its JSON representation.

# `new`

Construct a schema from a schema specification map.

The spec should have:
- "nodes" => list of {name, node_spec} tuples
- "marks" => (optional) list of {name, mark_spec} tuples
- "topNode" => (optional) name of the top node type, defaults to "doc"

# `node`

Create a node in this schema.

# `node_from_json`

Deserialize a node from its JSON representation.

# `node_type`

Look up a node type by name.

# `text`

Create a text node in the schema. Empty text nodes are not allowed.

---

*Consult [api-reference.md](api-reference.md) for complete listing*

---

# ProsemirrorEx.Model.Slice

Source: https://prosemirror-ex.hexdocs.pm/ProsemirrorEx.Model.Slice.md

# `ProsemirrorEx.Model.Slice`
[🔗](https://github.com/yammine/prosemirror_ex/blob/main/lib/prosemirror_ex/model/slice.ex#L1)

A slice represents a piece cut out of a larger document. It stores not only
a fragment, but also the depth up to which nodes on both sides are 'open'
(cut through).

Ported from ProseMirror's replace.ts Slice class.

# `t`

```elixir
@type t() :: %ProsemirrorEx.Model.Slice{
  content: term(),
  open_end: term(),
  open_start: term()
}
```

# `empty`

The empty slice.

# `eq`

Test whether this slice is equal to another slice.

# `from_json`

Deserialize a slice from its JSON representation.

# `insert_at`

Insert a fragment at the given position in this slice.

# `max_open`

Create a slice from a fragment by taking the maximum possible
open value on both sides of the fragment.

# `new`

Create a new slice.

# `remove_between`

Remove content between the given positions in this slice.

# `size`

The size this slice would add when inserted into a document.

# `to_json`

Convert a slice to a JSON-serializable representation.

# `to_string`

String representation of this slice.

---

*Consult [api-reference.md](api-reference.md) for complete listing*

---

# ProsemirrorEx.Transform.MapResult

Source: https://prosemirror-ex.hexdocs.pm/ProsemirrorEx.Transform.MapResult.md

# `ProsemirrorEx.Transform.MapResult`
[🔗](https://github.com/yammine/prosemirror_ex/blob/main/lib/prosemirror_ex/transform/map_result.ex#L1)

An object representing a mapped position with extra information.

Ports `MapResult` from prosemirror-transform/src/map.ts.

# `t`

```elixir
@type t() :: %ProsemirrorEx.Transform.MapResult{
  del_info: non_neg_integer(),
  pos: non_neg_integer(),
  recover: non_neg_integer() | nil
}
```

# `del_across`

Bitmask constant for deletion across.

# `del_after`

Bitmask constant for deletion after.

# `del_before`

Bitmask constant for deletion before.

# `del_side`

Bitmask constant for deletion on the queried side.

# `deleted?`

```elixir
@spec deleted?(t()) :: boolean()
```

Tells you whether the position was deleted, that is, whether the
step removed the token on the side queried (via the `assoc` argument)
from the document.

# `deleted_across?`

```elixir
@spec deleted_across?(t()) :: boolean()
```

Tells whether any of the steps mapped through deletes across the
position (including both the token before and after the position).

# `deleted_after?`

```elixir
@spec deleted_after?(t()) :: boolean()
```

True when the token after the mapped position was deleted.

# `deleted_before?`

```elixir
@spec deleted_before?(t()) :: boolean()
```

Tells you whether the token before the mapped position was deleted.

---

*Consult [api-reference.md](api-reference.md) for complete listing*

---

# ProsemirrorEx.Transform.Mappable

Source: https://prosemirror-ex.hexdocs.pm/ProsemirrorEx.Transform.Mappable.md

# `ProsemirrorEx.Transform.Mappable`
[🔗](https://github.com/yammine/prosemirror_ex/blob/main/lib/prosemirror_ex/transform/mappable.ex#L1)

Protocol for things that positions can be mapped through.

Ports the `Mappable` interface from prosemirror-transform/src/map.ts.

# `t`

```elixir
@type t() :: term()
```

All the types that implement this protocol.

# `map`

```elixir
@spec map(t(), non_neg_integer(), integer()) :: non_neg_integer()
```

Map a position through this object. `assoc` determines with which side
the position is associated (-1 or 1, defaults to 1), which determines
in which direction to move when a chunk of content is inserted at the
mapped position.

# `map_result`

```elixir
@spec map_result(t(), non_neg_integer(), integer()) ::
  ProsemirrorEx.Transform.MapResult.t()
```

Map a position, and return a MapResult containing additional
information about the mapping.

---

*Consult [api-reference.md](api-reference.md) for complete listing*

---

# ProsemirrorEx.Transform.Mapping

Source: https://prosemirror-ex.hexdocs.pm/ProsemirrorEx.Transform.Mapping.md

# `ProsemirrorEx.Transform.Mapping`
[🔗](https://github.com/yammine/prosemirror_ex/blob/main/lib/prosemirror_ex/transform/mapping.ex#L1)

A mapping represents a pipeline of zero or more StepMaps. It has special
provisions for losslessly handling mapping positions through a series of
steps in which some steps are inverted versions of earlier steps.

Ports `Mapping` from prosemirror-transform/src/map.ts.

# `t`

```elixir
@type t() :: %ProsemirrorEx.Transform.Mapping{
  from: non_neg_integer(),
  maps: [ProsemirrorEx.Transform.StepMap.t()],
  mirror: [non_neg_integer()] | nil,
  to: non_neg_integer()
}
```

# `append_map`

Add a step map to the end of this mapping. If `mirrors` is given,
it should be the index of the step map that is the mirror image of this one.

# `append_mapping`

Add all the step maps in a given mapping to this one (preserving mirroring information).

# `append_mapping_inverted`

Append the inverse of the given mapping to this one.

# `get_mirror`

Finds the offset of the step map that mirrors the map at the given offset.

# `invert`

Create an inverted version of this mapping.

# `map`

Map a position through this mapping.

# `map_result`

Map a position through this mapping, returning a MapResult.

# `new`

Create a new empty Mapping.

# `new`

Create a new Mapping with the given maps.

# `slice`

Create a mapping that maps only through a part of this one.

---

*Consult [api-reference.md](api-reference.md) for complete listing*

---

# ProsemirrorEx.Transform.Mark

Source: https://prosemirror-ex.hexdocs.pm/ProsemirrorEx.Transform.Mark.md

# `ProsemirrorEx.Transform.Mark`
[🔗](https://github.com/yammine/prosemirror_ex/blob/main/lib/prosemirror_ex/transform/mark.ex#L1)

Helper functions for adding and removing marks via Transform steps.

Ports `addMark`, `removeMark`, and `clearIncompatible` from
prosemirror-transform/src/mark.ts.

# `add_mark`

Add the given mark to inline content between `from` and `to`.

Walks the document, collecting RemoveMarkStep entries for any marks that
the new mark excludes, and AddMarkStep entries for ranges that need the
mark. Adjacent ranges are coalesced into a single step.

# `clear_incompatible`

Removes all marks and nodes from the content of the node at `pos` that
don't match the given new parent node type. Optionally accepts a starting
content match and a flag for clearing newlines.

# `remove_mark`

Remove marks from inline nodes between `from` and `to`.

When `mark` is a Mark, remove precisely that mark. When it is a MarkType,
remove all marks of that type. When it is nil, remove all marks.

---

*Consult [api-reference.md](api-reference.md) for complete listing*

---

# ProsemirrorEx.Transform.Replace

Source: https://prosemirror-ex.hexdocs.pm/ProsemirrorEx.Transform.Replace.md

# `ProsemirrorEx.Transform.Replace`
[🔗](https://github.com/yammine/prosemirror_ex/blob/main/lib/prosemirror_ex/transform/replace.ex#L1)

Fitter algorithm and replace helpers for fitting slices into document gaps.

Ports `replace.ts` from prosemirror-transform/src/replace.ts.

# `delete_range`

Smart delete that expands to cover parent nodes when appropriate.

# `insert_point`

Find a position at or around the given position where a node of the
given type can be inserted. Returns nil when no position was found.

# `replace_range`

WYSIWYG-aware replace. Expands/contracts the range for best structural fit.

# `replace_range_with`

WYSIWYG-aware single-node replacement.

# `replace_step`

'Fit' a slice into a given position in the document, producing a
step that inserts it. Will return nil if there's no meaningful way
to insert the slice here, or inserting it would be a no-op.

---

*Consult [api-reference.md](api-reference.md) for complete listing*

---

# ProsemirrorEx.Transform.Step

Source: https://prosemirror-ex.hexdocs.pm/ProsemirrorEx.Transform.Step.md

# `ProsemirrorEx.Transform.Step`
[🔗](https://github.com/yammine/prosemirror_ex/blob/main/lib/prosemirror_ex/transform/step.ex#L1)

A step object represents an atomic change. It generally applies only to the
document it was created for, since the positions stored in it will only make
sense for that document.

This module defines the behaviour that all step types must implement,
and provides a registry for JSON serialization/deserialization.

Ports `Step` from prosemirror-transform/src/step.ts.

# `apply`

```elixir
@callback apply(step :: term(), doc :: term()) :: ProsemirrorEx.Transform.StepResult.t()
```

Applies this step to the given document, returning a StepResult.

# `from_json`

```elixir
@callback from_json(schema :: term(), json :: map()) :: term()
```

Deserialize a step from its JSON representation.

# `invert`

```elixir
@callback invert(step :: term(), doc :: term()) :: term()
```

Create an inverted version of this step. Needs the document as it was before the step.

# `map`

```elixir
@callback map(step :: term(), mappable :: term()) :: term() | nil
```

Map this step through a mappable thing, returning a mapped step or nil.

# `merge`

```elixir
@callback merge(step :: term(), other :: term()) :: term() | nil
```

Try to merge this step with another one. Returns the merged step or nil.

# `step_map`

```elixir
@callback step_map(step :: term()) :: ProsemirrorEx.Transform.StepMap.t()
```

Get the step map that represents the changes made by this step.

# `to_json`

```elixir
@callback to_json(step :: term()) :: map()
```

Create a JSON-serializable representation of this step.

# `from_json`

Deserialize a step from its JSON representation.
Dispatches to the registered module based on the `stepType` field.

# `json_id`

Register a step module under a string ID for JSON serialization.
Raises if the ID is already registered.

---

*Consult [api-reference.md](api-reference.md) for complete listing*

---

# ProsemirrorEx.Transform.StepMap

Source: https://prosemirror-ex.hexdocs.pm/ProsemirrorEx.Transform.StepMap.md

# `ProsemirrorEx.Transform.StepMap`
[🔗](https://github.com/yammine/prosemirror_ex/blob/main/lib/prosemirror_ex/transform/step_map.ex#L1)

A map describing the deletions and insertions made by a step, which
can be used to find the correspondence between positions in the
pre-step version of a document and the same position in the post-step version.

Ports `StepMap` from prosemirror-transform/src/map.ts.

# `t`

```elixir
@type t() :: %ProsemirrorEx.Transform.StepMap{
  inverted: boolean(),
  ranges: [non_neg_integer()]
}
```

# `empty`

A StepMap that contains no changed ranges.

# `for_each`

Calls the given function on each of the changed ranges included in
this map. The function receives (old_start, old_end, new_start, new_end).
Returns a list of the results.

# `invert`

Create an inverted version of this map. The result can be used to
map positions in the post-step document to the pre-step document.

# `offset`

Create a map that moves all positions by offset `n` (which may be negative).

---

*Consult [api-reference.md](api-reference.md) for complete listing*

---

# ProsemirrorEx.Transform.StepResult

Source: https://prosemirror-ex.hexdocs.pm/ProsemirrorEx.Transform.StepResult.md

# `ProsemirrorEx.Transform.StepResult`
[🔗](https://github.com/yammine/prosemirror_ex/blob/main/lib/prosemirror_ex/transform/step_result.ex#L1)

The result of applying a step. Contains either a new document or a failure value.

Ports `StepResult` from prosemirror-transform/src/step.ts.

# `t`

```elixir
@type t() :: %ProsemirrorEx.Transform.StepResult{
  doc: ProsemirrorEx.Model.Node.t() | nil,
  failed: String.t() | nil
}
```

# `fail`

Create a failed step result.

# `from_replace`

Call `Node.replace` with the given arguments. Create a successful result
if it succeeds, and a failed one if it throws a `ReplaceError`.

# `ok`

Create a successful step result.

---

*Consult [api-reference.md](api-reference.md) for complete listing*

---

# ProsemirrorEx.Transform.Structure

Source: https://prosemirror-ex.hexdocs.pm/ProsemirrorEx.Transform.Structure.md

# `ProsemirrorEx.Transform.Structure`
[🔗](https://github.com/yammine/prosemirror_ex/blob/main/lib/prosemirror_ex/transform/structure.ex#L1)

Structural transform operations: lift, wrap, split, join, and
related utility functions.

Ports `structure.ts` from prosemirror-transform.

# `can_join`

Test whether the blocks before and after a given position can be joined.

# `can_split`

Check whether splitting at the given position is allowed.

# `drop_point`

Finds a position at or around the given position where the given
slice can be inserted. Will look at parent nodes' nearest boundary.
Returns nil when no position was found.

# `find_wrapping`

Try to find a valid way to wrap the content in the given range in a
node of the given type. May introduce extra nodes around and inside
the wrapper node. Returns nil if no valid wrapping could be found.

# `insert_point`

Try to find a point where a node of the given type can be inserted
near `pos`, by searching up the node hierarchy when `pos` itself
isn't a valid place but is at the start or end of a node.
Returns nil if no position was found.

# `join`

Join the blocks around the given position.

# `join_point`

Find an ancestor of the given position that can be joined to the
block before (or after if `dir` is positive). Returns the joinable
point, or nil.

# `lift`

Lift the content in the given range out of its parent to the
given target depth.

# `lift_target`

Try to find a target depth to which the content in the given range
can be lifted. Will not go across isolating parent nodes.
Returns an integer depth or nil.

# `set_block_type`

Set the type of all textblocks (partly) between `from` and `to` to the
given node type with the given attributes.

# `set_node_markup`

Change the type, attributes, and/or marks of the node at `pos`.
When `type` is nil, the existing node type is preserved.

# `split`

Split the node at the given position, creating new sibling nodes.

# `wrap`

Wrap the content in the given range in the given wrapper nodes.

---

*Consult [api-reference.md](api-reference.md) for complete listing*

---

# ProsemirrorEx.Transform.Transform

Source: https://prosemirror-ex.hexdocs.pm/ProsemirrorEx.Transform.Transform.md

# `ProsemirrorEx.Transform.Transform`
[🔗](https://github.com/yammine/prosemirror_ex/blob/main/lib/prosemirror_ex/transform/transform.ex#L1)

Abstraction to build up and track an array of steps representing a
document transformation.

Functions pattern-match on map keys rather than the %Transform{} struct
so that a future Transaction struct can reuse them.

Ports `Transform` from prosemirror-transform/src/transform.ts.

# `t`

```elixir
@type t() :: %ProsemirrorEx.Transform.Transform{
  doc: ProsemirrorEx.Model.Node.t(),
  docs: [ProsemirrorEx.Model.Node.t()],
  mapping: ProsemirrorEx.Transform.Mapping.t(),
  steps: [term()]
}
```

# `add_mark`

Add a mark to inline content between `from` and `to`.

# `before`

The starting document (before any steps were applied).

# `changed_range`

Return a single range, in post-transform document positions, that covers
all content changed by this transform. Returns nil if no replacements
are made. Note that this will ignore changes that add/remove marks without
replacing the underlying content.

# `clear_incompatible`

Removes all marks and nodes from the content of the node at `pos` that
don't match the given new parent node type.

# `delete`

Delete content between `from` and `to`.

# `delete_range`

Smart delete that expands to cover parent nodes when appropriate.

# `doc_changed?`

True when the document has been changed (when there are any steps).

# `insert`

Insert content at `pos`.

# `join`

Join the blocks around the given position.

# `lift`

Lift the content in the given range to the given target depth.

# `maybe_step`

Try to apply a step in this transformation, ignoring it if it fails.
Returns `{updated_tr, step_result}`.

# `new`

Create a new Transform starting with the given document.

# `remove_mark`

Remove marks from inline nodes between `from` and `to`. When `mark` is a
single mark, remove precisely that mark. When it is a mark type, remove all
marks of that type. When it is nil, remove all marks of any type.

# `replace`

Replace a range of the document with a slice.

# `replace_range`

WYSIWYG-aware replace across a range.

# `replace_range_with`

WYSIWYG-aware replace with a single node.

# `replace_with`

Replace a range of the document with a node or list of nodes.

# `set_block_type`

Set the type of all textblocks (partly) between `from` and `to`.

# `set_doc_attribute`

Set a document-level attribute.

# `set_node_attribute`

Set a single attribute on the node at pos.

# `set_node_markup`

Change the type, attributes, and/or marks of the node at `pos`.

# `split`

Split the node at the given position.

# `step`

Apply a new step in this transform, saving the result. Raises a
TransformError when the step fails.

# `wrap`

Wrap the content in the given range in the given wrapper nodes.

---

*Consult [api-reference.md](api-reference.md) for complete listing*

---
